messages:
jess: Quick note from onboarding: our JS sample shows fragment reordering when devs hit reconnect too fast (under ~200ms). Seen on Node SDK v0.9.x.

noah: Can you share a short repro?

jess: Steps: start stream, interrupt mid-chunk (ctrl-c), and reconnect immediately. Sometimes the last token is duplicated or a short fragment lands before the resume marker.

lin: Likely race between buffer flush debounce and auth-refresh retry path. We debounce flushes for 50ms; if resume happens within that window the buffered chunk may be replayed.

jess: Minimal curl repro:
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"reconnect test"}'
```

noah: CI log?

ci-bot: build/stream-e2e/5011 attached: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/5011 (flaky streaming)

lin: Quick mitigations: - add 200-300ms reconnect jitter in sample apps - flush buffers immediately during teardown (skip debounce) - surface a "resumed" SDK event with last-seq so apps can dedupe.

jess: I'll add a sample toggle that enables fast-reconnect stress and include a tiny dedupe snippet in onboarding docs. Also filing an internal issue.

noah: Filed: https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-3299. Plan: small server-side per-chunk seq tag + SDK resumed event + integration parity test node/python.

lin: Sounds good. We should keep the workaround in onboarding notes until server+SDK patch lands. :thumbsup:
